question.problem:
Suppose we take a random sample of size $n=80$ from a population where $42%$ of the population has a particular characteristic. Find a normal approximation for the probability that more than $35%$ of the sample has the characteristic. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.4\,$ | $\,0.0735\,$ | $\,0.0721\,$ | $\,0.0708\,$ | $\,0.0694\,$ | $\,0.0681\,$ |
| $\,-1.3\,$ | $\,0.0885\,$ | $\,0.0869\,$ | $\,0.0853\,$ | $\,0.0838\,$ | $\,0.0823\,$ |
| $\,-1.2\,$ | $\,0.1056\,$ | $\,0.1038\,$ | $\,0.1020\,$ | $\,0.1003\,$ | $\,0.0985\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=80,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.42.$

Now, since

$$
np=80(0.42)=33.6>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=80(1-0.42)=46.4>5,
$$

and $n=80$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.42,\frac{0.42(1-0.42)}{80}) \\  & ∼N(0.42,0.003\,045).\end{aligned}
$$

The probability we wish to find is
$P(\overset{^}{\,p}>0.35).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{^}{\,p}>0.35) & =P(Z>\frac{0.35-0.42}{\sqrt{0.003\,045}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>-1.27) \\  & =1-P(Z<-1.27) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.27).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-1.27) & =0.1020.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{^}{\,p}>0.35) & =1-Φ(-1.27) \\  & =1-0.1020 \\  & =0.8980.\end{aligned}
$$
